thread.title: Sen. Marco Rubio rolls out online-privacy legislation

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: Sen. Marco Rubio rolls out online-privacy legislation
text:
Sen. Marco Rubio on Wednesday introduced legislation that would deliver a national consumer data-privacy law, saying his bill should prevent outrages along the lines of Facebook’s Cambridge Analytica scandal .
The Florida Republican’s American Data Dissemination Act would require the Federal Trade Commission to submit detailed recommendations for privacy requirements that Congress could impose on tech companies. If Congress then failed to act on the recommendations within two years, Rubio’s bill would enable the FTC to put into effect its own rules.
“It is important Congress legislate the new rules of the road, but we should use the non-partisan expertise from the agency of jurisdiction to ensure lawmakers make informed decisions to properly protect consumers,” Rubio said in a Hill op-ed about the ADD Act.
“My bill also takes important precautions to ensure it does not entrench large, incumbent corporations,” he wrote. Tech giants such as the FAANG companies — Facebook FB, -0.95% , Apple AAPL, +1.22% , Amazon AMZN, +0.55% , Netflix NFLX, -0.92% and Alphabet’s GOOG, +0.35% GOOGL, +0.28% Google — “would welcome cumbersome regulations that prevent startups and smaller competitors from challenging the FAANG’s current dominance.”
The text of Rubio’s bill says it “shall supersede” state laws, meaning it would override California’s new, tough data-privacy law . Big tech companies and internet service providers have said they want federal legislation that would preempt the Golden State’s strict new rules. Meanwhile, some activists and Democratic lawmakers have signaled they won’t support federal legislation if it weakens efforts like California’s.
Additional privacy bills look set to get introduced later this year, as other lawmakers, such as Sen. Richard Blumenthal , the Connecticut Democrat, have indicated they aim to unveil legislation that could draw bipartisan support. Rubio’s legislation follows related prior bills, such as a bipartisan Social Media Privacy Protection and Consumer Rights Act that was rolled out last year but didn’t get much traction.
Victor Reklaitis Victor Reklaitis is MarketWatch's Money & Politics reporter and is based in Washington, D.C. Follow him on Twitter @VicRek .
